newsitem.title: USA: Payless Cashways files Ch. 11 bankruptcy.
newsitem.headline: Payless Cashways files Ch. 11 bankruptcy.

text.p: Payless Cashways Inc, a building materials retailer, said Monday it has filed a voluntary petition to reorganize under Chapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy code in order to facilitate a debt restructuring.
The company also said it plans to close 29 stores and cut 1,900 positions, while implementing about a 100-person reduction of staff at the company's headquarters and regional administrative centers.

The company has also received a commitment from a group of financial institutions led by Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, the company's agent bank, for $125 million in debtor-in-possession financing, Payless Cashways said.

The post-petition financing, which is subject to court approval, is expected to provide adequate funding for all post-petition trade and employee obligations, as well as the company's ongoing operating needs during the restructuring process, the company said.
The restructuring plan has the required support of the company's bank group, Payless Cashways said.

The filing of the bankruptcy petition will allow Payless Cashways to continue to operate its business without interruption while it obtains necessary approval of its plan of reorganization, the company said.

"Key to improving Payless Cashways' competitive position is to improve our balance sheet," David Stanley, chairman and chief executive officer, said in a news release. "The company has operated with an extremely burdensome level of debt which has limited capital expenditures during a period of unprecedented competitive pressure."
The company has also secured a commitment for $150 million of financing from a group of lenders for use upon completion of the reorganization," Stanley said.
The company was unlikely to be able to meet the requirements of its principal credit agreements at the end of the current fiscal year, Stanley said.
As a result, the company has been working with its senior lenders over the past several weeks in an attempt to restructure its debt.
The company has been in contact with many of its suppliers and believes they will continue to support Payless Cashways during the reorganization period, Stanley said.

Daily operations at the company's 165 ongoing stores will continue, and policies regarding returns, exchanges, special orders, deposits, credit purchases and gift certificates will remain unchanged, the company said.
